Last generated at: `r Sys.time()`

## Purpose

This is a quality-control / quality-assurance report generated by the Moseley Bioinformatics Lab for the Metabolomics Workbench (MW) analysis {analysis_id} ([link]({analysis_link})) from study {study_id} ([link]({study_link})).
We provide the [Metabolomics Workbench information](#metabolomics-workbench-information) taken from the various MW data blocks, and then various measures of QC/QA that we have found useful to evaluate before analyzing data.

These include:

* [calculating the percent missingness](#missing-values-as-result-of-left-censorship), and whether the missing values are likely due to left-censorship;
* [plotting](#raw-data-boxplot) the raw and median normalized log-abundances in each sample;
* [calculating relative standard deviations (RSD)](#rsd-raw-and-normalized) or coefficient of variation of features within each group, and comparing raw to normalized values;
* Evaluating the sample grouping by:
  * sample-sample correlations from information-content-informed Kendall-tau,
  * median ICI-Kt within known sample groups, 
  * comparing within factors median ICI-Kt to between factors median ICI-Kt,
  * factor runs from the hierarchical clustering,
  * principal component analysis (PCA), 
  * ANOVA of sample PC scores *vs* individual sample factors.
* for these different sets of samples:
  * [all samples](#all-samples);
  * [removing outliers](#outliers-removed);
  * [removing QC samples](#quality-control-samples-removed);
  * [removing both outliers and QC samples](#outliers-and-quality-control-samples-removed)

It is important to note that if there are no outlier or QC samples, then the results in subsequent sections will be identical to **all samples**.
However, this is an automated analysis and report, so they are all presented, regardless of the presence of outlier or QC samples.

If a section is blank, that likely means there were no samples left to use to create graphs or tables, and the code cell was not evaluated.

## Important terms

* Metabolomics Workbench: the data repository where the data came from.
* Project: an overarching question or line of investigation.
* Study: one particular set of analyses. There may be multiple studies in a project.
* Analysis: one run of analysis, such as one type of chromatography, or instrumentation (NMR, MS, specific polarity, LC vs GC, etc). There are one or more analyses per study.
* Sample: one biological unit in an analysis.
* Feature: a measured entity within the instrumentation, within one analysis. This may be a named metabolite, a binned range in NMR, a set of M/Z locations, or a combination of chromatography peak range and M/Z for chromatographic MS.

## Quality Control / Quality Assurance

### Missing Values as Result of Left Censorship

* % Missing Values: `r format(use_pca$left_censorship$perc_missing, digits = 2)`.

Left censorship test results:

```{r}
#| label: tbl-left-censorship-results
#| tbl-cap: Number of non-missing values that are below the median for each group (success) vs number of missing (trials).
#| message: true
if (!is.null(use_pca$left_censorship[["lc_test"]])) {
  use_pca$left_censorship$lc_test$values |>
    dplyr::select(class, trials, success) |>
    dplyr::transmute(factors = class, trials = trials, success = success) |>
    gt::gt()
} else {
  message("No left-censorship test results.")
}
```

* Binomial test result:

```{r}
#| label: left-censorship-test
#| message: true
if (!is.null(use_pca$left_censorship[["lc_test"]])) {
  use_pca$left_censorship$lc_test$binomial_test
} else {
  message("No left-censroship test results.")
}
```

### Numbers of Samples

```{r}
#| label: tbl-sample-summary
#| tbl-cap: Number of different types of samples.
sample_info = get_vardata(use_pca$abundance)
tibble::tibble(
  `Sample Type` = c("Overall", "Experimental", "QC", "Outliers"),
  N = c(
    nrow(sample_info),
    sum(sample_info$experiment_or_qc %in% "experiment"),
    sum(sample_info$experiment_or_qc %in% "qc"),
    sum(sample_info$outlier)
  )
) |>
  gt::gt()
```
